thread:
anika: Heads-up: RFC follow-up — proposing autoscaler safety + fallback rules for dedicated GPU pools. TL;DR: tighten hysteresis, add cost-smoothing, and a deterministic fallback lane before evictions. Feedback?

brian: Nice. Can you sketch the operator flow? Specifically worried about oscillation when a tenant spikes then cools quickly.

anika: Sure. Rough flow: 1) metrics aggregated w/ smoothing window (configurable) 2) admission checks against reservation + burst credits 3) if admission fails, try fallback lane (lower-SLO model variant) 4) if fallback not available, enqueue prewarm request or return 429 depending on tenant tier

yara: What are we considering for "smoothing window" and hysteresis params? Short window avoids latency but causes churn.

anika: Proposal: default smoothing_window = 60s (exponential moving average), hysteresis_open = 90s, hysteresis_close = 180s. Make all tenant-configurable with org-level sane defaults.

brian: Sounds reasonable. We should also gate scale-up rate to avoid immediate full-scale blasts. e.g., max_scale_up_pct = 50% per 60s.

anika: Agreed. Also adding a token-bucket style cost-smoothing for burst credits so short spikes use credits but long sustained load pays for capacity.

ashley: How does fallback lane look in config? Example YAML?

anika: Example config snippet:

```
# autoscaler policy for dedicated pool (example)
policy:
  smoothing_window_seconds: 60
  hysteresis:
    open_seconds: 90
    close_seconds: 180
  scale_limits:
    max_scale_up_pct_per_window: 50
    max_scale_down_pct_per_window: 30
  fallback:
    enabled: true
    lane: "burst-lane-quantized"
    model_variant: "gpt-medium-8q"
    max_fallback_concurrency_per_tenant: 10
  burst_credits:
    bucket_size: 300
    refill_rate_per_min: 60
  prewarm:
    reserve_count: 2
    ttl_seconds: 600
```

solomon: Two concerns: 1) how do we coordinate fallback across regions to avoid double-counting credits? 2) what are the correctness guarantees for prewarm TTL causing double-provisioning?

anika: For region coordination we keep per-region credit buckets and a global cap that is only consulted during cross-region failover. Prewarm TTL is conservative; operator will track active leases and de-duplicate requests using the tenant request-id.

brian: Runbook snippet for when autoscaler overscales or oscillates? We should add clear pager steps.

anika: Draft runbook blurb:

- symptom: rapid scale-up/down >3 times within 10m or token costs spike >x%
- immediate check: `kubectl get pods -n dedicated-pools` & `redwoodctl autoscaler status --pool <pool>`
- mitigation: flip `policy.scale_limits.max_scale_up_pct_per_window` to 25% and enable `policy.force_stable=true` (operator will hold target replicas fixed)
- fallback rollback: force-route high-priority tenants to dedicated fallback lane by setting `tenant.spec.fallback_preference: dedicated`
- post-incident: capture metric window, attach sample of request timestamps and tenant IDs, open follow-up RFC

yara: +1 on adding a "force_stable" switch. Also we should emit a synthetic metric `autoscaler.hysteresis_state{pool}` for dashboards.

anika: Will add. Also proposing that deploy-bot blocks autoscaler config changes during canary rollouts (safety).

deploy-bot: FYI — I can add a pre-deploy webhook to block policy flips for pools tagged `canary:true`. /cc @anika

ashley: Who owns the operator changes? I can take the fallback admission flow and tests.

anika: Thanks — assign to ashley for fallback admission + tests. @brian can you take rate-limiting + smoothing logic? @solomon can you own cross-region credits and de-dupe logic? I'll own runbook + console metrics.

oncall-bot: Reminder: any change to autoscaler defaults requires SLO approval and a staged rollout (50% of pools -> 100%).

brian: A couple of open questions to capture in follow-up RFC: 1) default credit economics (how many minutes free) 2) tiered fallback behavior for enterprise vs free tenants 3) telemetry labels we need for debugging (request-id, tenant-tier, admission-path)

anika: I'll draft RFC with those questions and a sample rollout plan. Thanks all — will post the draft by EOD. :thumbsup:
